page.overview:
What is Rhosgobel?

Rhosgobel, also known as Brownhay, was the location of the old home of the wizard Radagast the Brown.

Rhosgobel was said to have been located between the Great Carrock and the Menn-i-Naugrim of the western borders of the Gladden Fields.

At some point in time after his arrival in Middle-earth around the year 1000 of the late Third Age the wizard Radagast made a home for himself at Rhosgobel, where he continued to dwell until at least sometime after the year 2941 according to the wizard Gandalf the Grey.

After the Council of Elrond, some scouts from Rivendell (Elrond's sons Elladan and Elrohir) crossed over the Misty Mountains using the pass at the sources of the Gladden River to come down into Rhovanion and over the Gladden Fields to reach Rhosgobel, but they found that Radagast was not there.
